p.x:
There is a small café near my school. I go there every Saturday with my friends. The café has big windows and lots of plants.
I always order an iced coffee because the weather is hot. My friend Ploy likes hot chocolate with cream. The owner pours the drinks into big mugs. She also sells biscuits, and they are delicious.
The owner buys coffee beans from farms in the north of Thailand. Behind the counter, there is a big silver kettle. The café is my favourite place to relax.

Around the world, people are divided into tea lovers and coffee lovers. In Britain, tea is a national habit. Many people make it with a teabag in a mug, but some still use a teapot and serve it in a cup on a saucer. A cup of tea with a biscuit is a classic afternoon break.
In Japan, green tea is part of daily life. People sip it slowly, and it is less bitter than coffee. Herbal teas, made from flowers or plants, are popular with people who want to avoid caffeine.
Coffee, however, has become more fashionable, especially among young people. In a modern café, a skilled barista can make an espresso, a latte or a cappuccino with thick foam on top. Some customers add sweet syrup, while others prefer their coffee black. At home, many people still drink instant coffee because it is quick and cheap. Those who drink coffee late in the day often choose decaf so they can sleep.
The coffee shop has also become a social place. Friends meet up there to catch up, and students study for hours with one drink. In Thailand, bubble tea shops are everywhere. And for many people, nothing beats the aroma of freshly roasted coffee in the morning. Some even grind the beans and brew their coffee at home.

Coffee and tea are among the most widely consumed drinks on earth, yet few drinkers think about where they come from. Most coffee is grown in tropical countries such as Brazil, Vietnam and Colombia, while tea comes mainly from China, India and Sri Lanka. On large plantations and small family farms alike, the work is hard, and many growers earn only a tiny share of the price customers pay in cafés.
The journey from plant to cup involves several stages. Coffee cherries are picked, dried and processed to remove the seeds, which are then roasted. The roast determines much of the flavour: lighter roasts tend to have more acidity and fruity notes, while darker roasts are richer and more bitter. Many roasters create a blend of beans from different regions to achieve a balanced taste. A true connoisseur can identify a coffee's origin, its body and its aftertaste in a single sip.
Tea, too, varies enormously depending on how it is processed and how long the leaves are left to infuse. In Thailand, a popular version is cha yen, strong black tea sweetened with sugar and condensed milk and served over ice.
Scientists have studied both drinks extensively. Caffeine increases alertness and concentration for several hours, although too much can leave people feeling jittery or unable to sleep. Tea, particularly green tea, contains antioxidants that may protect cells from damage, although researchers warn against exaggerated health claims.
